It notes (p. ~316) that Oldendorp 'classified his informants' languages by creating word lists' but gives no words and no remark on pronunciation, accent or tone. 0 hits for tone/tonal/accent/pitch/prosod/syllable/phonolog/vowel; the one 'stress' hit is the verb 'he stressed…

sources.note: No phonology content. Ethnographic account only (scarification, neighbours Kanga/Mandinga/Amina, warfare, religion: 'Gott hiess in ihrem Lande Jankombum.. Teufel, nennen ihn Didi', burial, priests, poison ordeal). Adds two lexical items in context (Jankombum 'God', Didi 'devil', both said to be shared with Amina) but no remark on pronunciation, accent or tone. Confirms that even the unabridged Oldendorp edition's Mangree account carries no phonological description.

sources.note: No phonology of Mangree. The only Mangree content is a classificatory remark (p. 320): 'OLDENDORPs Sprachproben stimmen mit Kru in Kanga und meist auch in Gien, in Mangree nur teilweise; die betr. Negerin mischte auch zwei Asante-Wörter (für Gott und Kopf) und ein portugiesisches (pikkenine für Kind) mit ein.' i.e. the Mangree words agree with Kru only partly and include two Asante loans and one Portuguese word. (The article does remark on Kru vowel qualities, not on Mangree.)
